sections.title: God's Sovereignty and Judgment
observations: The psalm opens with a declaration of God's greatness and the acknowledgment of His sovereignty over all creation. The psalmist praises God for His wondrous deeds and recognizes that it is God who establishes the right time for judgment.

This section emphasizes that God is not only aware of the injustices in the world but is actively involved in the administration of justice. The imagery of God holding a cup of wine symbolizes His judgment against the wicked.

sections.title: The Fate of the Wicked
observations: The psalmist contrasts the fate of the wicked with that of the righteous. The wicked are depicted as those who will drink from the cup of God's wrath, while the righteous will be vindicated.
This section serves as a warning to those who oppose God and His people, highlighting the certainty of divine retribution.

importantVerses.commentary: When God says, 'At the appointed time, I will judge with equity,' it underscores the certainty and fairness of God's judgment, reminding believers that justice will ultimately prevail.
The imagery of the cup in God's hand signifies His control over judgment and the fate of the wicked, illustrating that their downfall is orchestrated by divine authority.

questions: What does this psalm teach us about the nature of God's judgment?
How can we find comfort in the assurance that God will ultimately bring justice?
In what ways does the imagery of the cup enhance our understanding of God's wrath and mercy?
